title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page continues §3, 'Théorie de déformations pour les schémas abéliens', of what appears to be Grothendieck's plan or exposé for a seminar on crystalline Dieudonné theory. The setting is the nilpotent crystalline site; no prime is privileged. For an abelian scheme f: A → S, the contravariant crystal is D*(A) = R^1 f_{cris*} O_{A_cris}. Its value on a locally nilpotent PD-thickening S' of S is computed as H^1_DR(A'/S') for any abelian scheme A' lifting A to S'. Two inputs make this work. First, such lifts exist when S is affine; this is Grothendieck's unobstructedness of deformations of abelian schemes, cited via Mumford's GIT. Second, the base-change and crystalline machinery ('le tapis de la cohomologie cristalline') shows that H^1_DR(A'/S') is independent of the lift up to canonical isomorphism. On S itself, the Hodge filtration 0 → f_*Ω^1_{A/S} → H^1_DR(A/S) → R^1 f_* O_A → 0 is read as 0 → ω_A (= dual of the tangent space t_A) → D*(A)_S → t_{A*} (= Lie of the dual abelian scheme) → 0. This sequence is functorial in A and compatible with base change, so D* factors through filtered crystals: locally free crystals with a two-step filtration whose graded pieces are locally free. The resulting theorem, the deformation theorem for abelian schemes, says the following. For a locally nilpotent PD-thickening S' of S, the functor A' ↦ (A' ⊗ S, Fil^1 = ω_{A'} ⊂ H^1_DR(A'/S') = D*(A)_{S'}) is an equivalence. Its target is the category of pairs (A, Fil^1), where A is an abelian scheme over S and Fil^1 is a locally direct-summand submodule of D*(A)_{S'} lifting ω_A. In words, lifting A amounts to lifting its Hodge filtration. Part (b) begins a second interpretation via the universal vector extension E(A), viewed as a crystal in smooth groups (Mazur–Messing style); per the next page, this is meant to construct a quasi-inverse.
errors: No substantive error. Several hypotheses are left implicit: PD-compatibility with the base, the locally nilpotent PD condition, and the fact that the cited existence of lifts is Grothendieck's theorem as reproduced in GIT rather than a result of Mumford. Independence of the lift is asserted only up to isomorphism; a transitive system of canonical isomorphisms is needed and is addressed on the next page.
The words 'pour S affine' suffice for existence of a lift. Globally, lifts need not exist, but the crystal is still defined by gluing; this is implicit.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean draft of the Grothendieck–Messing theorem for abelian schemes, which is well known and credited (ICM 1970 announcement, Messing 1972, Mazur–Messing 1974). It has historical interest as a seminar draft but adds no new mathematics.
